cells.tense: You can let something fall among the people you love and stay close as it lands.
cells.act: keep the session even when it feels pointless
cells.ask: Keep a shared rhythm with the people close to you going at the same hour this season, including the weeks it seems to be carrying nothing.
cells.core:
Something you all carry together — a habit, an arrangement, the way you talk with each other — can go when the moment shows it stopped holding. You don't have to force it down or hurry to patch it. You stay with these people through the landing, and the connection takes the weight.

Steadiness is what carries you. Keep a shared rhythm with them going at the same hour this season, through the weeks it seems to be carrying nothing. That repeated beat is what lets the bigger thing break without the ground going with it. You get to feel with people and keep your feet under you at once — same you, same rhythm, both sides of it.
cells.sheetLine: You can let something fall and stay close while it lands.
cells.verb: letting what can't hold fall away, suddenly and cleanly
cells.place: among the people you're close to

cells.tense: You will tear things down among the people close to you before anything has shown you it should fall.
cells.act: learn how the people before you did it
cells.ask: Ask one of the people close to you how a shared thing has actually been for them lately, and sit with their answer before you decide what goes.
cells.core:
Around the people you're close to, things get cleared out before anyone has shown you they can't hold — a plan, a way you meet, a habit. Each clearing reads as honesty from where you stand, and you're standing a season on from the others at the table. From their side, nothing gets to mean anything long enough to be missed.

What's thin is the connection, not the nerve. Before the next clear-out, ask one of them how a shared thing has actually been for them lately, and sit with their answer before you decide. You're not checking permission; you're letting the shared part be shared again. They get to feel seen, you get to feel with them, and what really needs to go can still go — with both of you there when it does.
cells.sheetLine: You're clearing before anything's had room to mean.
cells.verb: letting what can't hold fall away, suddenly and cleanly
cells.place: among the people you're close to

cells.tense: A structure had stopped holding among the people you love, and you are still propping it up.
cells.act: build the smallest structure that holds it
cells.ask: Give one stale way of meeting among the people close to you a date, a length, a place to stop — a shape that holds it without your arms.
cells.core:
Something you share with people has already stopped holding, and you're keeping it moving with both arms. The weekly thing still happens, the old arrangement still stands, and none of it gives anything to anyone — including you. From where you sit, ending it feels like losing the connection. It's the other way: you're spending all your energy on a frame where there's nobody left to feel with.

Put a shape around it instead of a wall. Give one stale way of meeting a date, a length, a place to stop — a shape that holds it without your arms. When the container is solid, the relationship can move with the people it's actually about. Nothing gets killed. The weight comes off your hands, and it doesn't land back on you.
cells.sheetLine: You're still propping up what's already stopped holding.
cells.verb: letting what can't hold fall away, suddenly and cleanly
cells.place: among the people you're close to

cells.tense: Something is about to fall among the people close to you, and you haven't noticed you're the one holding it up.
cells.act: go where the feeling is already pulling
cells.ask: Follow what already pulls you toward one of the people close to you — reach out, make the plan, say the thing — before you weigh whether it makes sense.
cells.core:
Something among the people close to you is set to fall — a plan, a habit, the shape of how you show up — and you're not bracing for it or waiting it out. From inside, it looks like getting on with the group. From outside, your grip is the only thing keeping it standing. Ask what's about to break and you'd report nothing on your screen yet. The breaking is being arranged. The one arranging it is turned away.

Start from what pulls you, before the analysis. Follow what already draws you toward one of these people — reach out, make the plan, say the thing — before you weigh whether it makes sense. Wanting from the people close to you is simpler than sorting what to keep, and it's what makes the deciding come out right. When the false part drops, the pull is still there. You'll know where you stand.
cells.sheetLine: Something's about to fall, and you're the last to notice.
cells.verb: letting what can't hold fall away, suddenly and cleanly
cells.place: among the people you're close to

Reader's objection: 'Nothing has actually fallen — you're telling me I'm propping up something that's fine.' The ask survives being wrong, because a small repeated practice readies the person for whatever does or doesn't fall. Sentence that serves me more than them: any version of 'the collapse already happened and you're the last to know' — cut; the core says what they can see from where they stand. Also cool the Too Much cell: 'you teach change' would flatter the reader and put a method in her mouth — the ask reads something from the people she's handing it to, nothing promoted.
